In summary, our research is concerned with

the production of radioactive 44Ti, which has been observed to be synthesized in core-collapse supernova explosions, and is an important tracer of the explosion mechanism and the nucleosynthesis in the innermost ejecta.
the nuclear physics of 44Ti and its implications for supernovae and their remnants.
understanding and improving the uncertainties in 44Ti production, which is an important diagnostic of supernovae and their explosion mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
44Ti production is not yet understood to the degree that would be required to make a definitive comparison between theory and observation, and that further work is required to reduce uncertainties.
the 44Ti abundance is not yet known to a level that can be used as a reliable tracer of stellar physics in supernovae.
44Ti production is sensitive to nuclear reaction rates and that the 40Ca(alpha, gamma)44Ti and 44Ti(alpha, p)47 V rates should be measured to higher precision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 44Ti yield in supernova models is not only sensitive to the peak temperature and density of an explosion, but it is also sensitive to the reaction rates of the 44Ca(α,γ)44Ti and 44Ti( α,p)47V reactions.
the current uncertainty of the 44Ca(α,γ)44Ti reaction rate could be reduced to a level of 20% by a combination of a new experimental measurement and a more detailed theoretical calculation.
the 40Ca+α reaction rate is the most important reaction rate for 44Ti synthesis and that the current uncertainty for this reaction is too large to draw firm conclusions regarding the 44Ti abundance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncertainty in 44Ca(α, γ)44Ti is now comparable to that of the 44Sc(γ, n)44Ti reaction.
the uncertainty of 44Ti yields in the α-rich freezeouts can be reduced by improving the precision of the 40Ca+α reaction rate.
the 44Ti production rate is sensitive to the reaction rates of the two reactions considered, but that this sensitivity is highly model dependent.
